docs: The input as three 4×4 channel grids, red, green and blue, one number per cell, with the pixel being normalized outlined. Time walks the pixels row by row; every pixel's three channels are done in one step.

μ and σ drawn once: three cells each, one per channel, not 48. The leader from the current pixel reaches its channel's cells by the index projection (h, w, c) ↦ c; nothing is ever copied out to the image's shape.
z as three channel grids filling in one pixel per step, each finished cell a bar for its value: right of centre positive, left negative, in units of the channel's spread.

Broadcasting as an index map: the image's index (h, w, c) is sent to c alone, and μ[c], σ[c] are read from 3-tuples. The runtime evaluates (x[h,w,c] − μ[c]) / σ[c] at every position with no 4×4×3 copy of μ or σ ever allocated: semantic broadcasting, index mapping, no materialization.
